title: Trinity Rodman Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Discover how Trinity Rodman's salary compares to Australian award rates. Learn to convert hourly pay to annual using the 38-hour week, including tax and super.
salarySummary: Using the standard 38-hour week and 52-week year, any hourly rate can be converted to annual gross pay; for example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour yields $52,270.72 per year.

faqs.q: What is the formula to convert an hourly rate to annual pay?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross salary.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect the calculation?
faqs.a: Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, if the base rate is $26.44 per hour, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour. You should enter the base rate into the calculator and check the casual loading box to apply the 25% addition.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate shown?
faqs.a: No. The super guarantee is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. For 2026–27, the super rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. It is not part of the cash hourly rate you receive.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Conversion

To convert an hourly rate to annual pay, multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked each week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours. This is the ordinary full-time week used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The formula is simple: **hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross salary**.

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38‑hour week, as published by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For casual employees, a 25% loading applies, bringing the casual minimum rate to $33.05 per hour.

## Trinity Rodman Salary in Context

While the exact figure for Trinity Rodman’s salary is not available in the search results, the conversion method applies to any hourly rate. If you know her reported earnings in US dollars, you can use our calculator to see the Australian equivalent. For example, a rate of $40 per hour gives an annual gross of $79,040 (38 hours × 52 weeks). After income tax and the Medicare levy, the estimated take‑home pay is about $63,227 per year, or $1,215 per week.

Award rates vary by industry and occupation. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database provides detailed minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each award. Always check the specific award that applies to your job.

## The Fortnight and Tax

A fortnight is simply two weeks. If your weekly gross is $1,520 (at $40 per hour), your fortnightly gross is $3,040. Many employers pay fortnightly, so knowing this figure helps with budgeting.

Income tax for 2026–27 uses the resident tax‑free threshold: nil on the first $18,200, then 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Using the $40‑per‑hour example, the estimated annual tax is $14,232 and Medicare is $1,580.80, leaving a net of $63,227.20. These estimates assume you claim the tax‑free threshold and have private hospital cover (avoiding the Medicare levy surcharge).

## Casual Loading and Award Rates

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. When using the calculator, enter the **base rate** (without loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox. The tool will add 25% automatically. For award‑covered employees, the base rate is the minimum rate in the relevant award. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides list these rates for every award.

Award rates are higher than the National Minimum Wage in many industries. For example, the Supported Employment Services Award has its own classification rates. Always refer to the correct award or enterprise agreement.

## Superannuation

The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings for 2026–27, paid on top of your cash salary. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year; super is not paid on earnings above that cap. For a $40‑per‑hour employee, the employer contributes an extra $9,484.80 per year (12% of $79,040). This is separate from your take‑home pay.

## Using the Calculator

Visit [the timesheet](/) to input your hourly rate. The calculator assumes a 38‑hour week and 52 weeks per year. You can adjust the hours if you work part‑time. The results show gross annual pay, estimated tax, Medicare, net pay, and employer super. For award‑specific rates, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data).

For more on minimum wage, see [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage). To understand your take‑home pay after tax, visit [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home). Information on super and salary packaging is at [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Important Notes

This conversion is an estimate. It assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates or allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. Always check your payslip and notice of assessment for official figures.
